manifest.title: OpenCode
manifest.tagline: Open source AI coding agent, in your browser
manifest.description:
## About

[OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) is an open source AI coding agent. This package runs the OpenCode
server with its web UI, so you can plan, write and run code from any browser, with sessions,
projects and credentials stored on your Cloudron.

## Features

* Full OpenCode web UI: sessions, diffs, file browser and a built-in terminal
* Works with Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter, local models and many other providers
* MCP servers, custom agents, commands, skills and plugins
* Cloudron login in front of the app (optional), with automatic sign-in to OpenCode
* Projects live in `/app/data/workspace` and are included in Cloudron backups
* Ships with git, GitHub CLI, Node.js, Python with uv, ripgrep and fd

## Security

OpenCode can run any command with the permissions of the app. Treat access to this app like shell
access to its container, and only grant it to people you trust.
manifest.postInstallMessage:
OpenCode can run arbitrary commands inside this app. Only give access to people you trust.

<sso>
Sign in with your Cloudron account and OpenCode opens straight away.
</sso>

<nosso>
OpenCode is protected by its own server password. To read it, open the app's Web Terminal and run:

```
opencode service get password
```

Then choose **Use password** on the OpenCode connect screen.
</nosso>

Next, connect a model provider under **Settings → Providers**, or add API keys to `/app/data/env.sh`
and restart the app. Put projects in `/app/data/workspace`.

connect-provider.message: Connect a model provider: open **Settings → Providers** in the web UI, or put API keys in `/app/data/env.sh` and restart the app.

server-password.message: Get the server password from the Web Terminal with `opencode service get password`, then choose **Use password** on the OpenCode connect screen.

manifest.changelog:
* Health check now confirms the API and database answer, and reveals only up or down
* OpenCode server logs appear in the Cloudron app log
* Keep package manager caches, the OpenCode log file and reference repo checkouts out of backups
* Releases go through a testing stage before they are published
